intended_use: Exploratory flat-printed in-layer pre-peak tensile sensitivity; not a fracture, compression, or build-Z model

screening_isotropic.nu_provenance: User-supplied initialization prior; not measured in the cited dataset
screening_isotropic.selection_reason: Isotropic has the lowest BIC; source placement groups do not map completely to local material axes

raw_curve_extraction.fit: affine ordinary least squares after exact-row deduplication

directional_observations.interpretation: Z-upright loading is consistent with the build direction; the other placement groups cannot be uniquely assigned to local bead and in-layer transverse axes from this source.

reported_strength_reference.interpretation: Reference limit only. The linear-elastic solver does not predict failure.

sources.note: Reported overall elastic modulus and tensile strength; associated raw workbook has documented label/count conflicts.
Density, Poisson ratios, shear moduli, and TDS-style directional initialization values supplied in the project brief.

limitations: The raw workbook has 22 curves while the article claims 21.
Source placement labels and summary-workbook specimen labels conflict.
Only Z-upright has a defensible direct build-axis interpretation.
Poisson ratios and shear moduli remain project priors.
No compression, flexural, fatigue, creep, fracture, or held-out component measurements are available for this exact material source.
The J2 flow assumption is not identified by uniaxial tensile data.
Plastic incompressibility and equal tension/compression yield are unverified for printed PLA.
Z-upright curves are excluded from the in-layer hardening aggregate.
The card stops at the last strain with at least 80% non-Z pre-peak coverage.
No post-peak softening, necking, damage, fracture, rate, temperature, or cyclic behavior is represented.

plastic_isotropic.derivation: zero-shifted pre-peak engineering curves; conditional median with >=80% specimen coverage; 0.2% offset yield; true stress and logarithmic strain conversion
